tagline.text: A viewdeck above sea cliffs overlooking waves and rolling green hills on the western coast

location.label: Location
location.text: Top of the Chawa winding road, Barangay Hanib, along the Basco National Road in Mahatao, Batanes

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100–1,500 (per person; tricycle or South Batan tour, excluding flights and lodging)

children.text: Chawa Viewdeck is a viewdeck on a cliff beside the national road in the Mahatao section of southern Batan Island. The western sea, cliffs and rolling green hills spread out in a single frame, and a path of about 100 concrete steps leads down to the shore.

Chawa Viewdeck sits on a cliff beside the national road in the Mahatao section of southern Batan Island, the main island of Batanes. Its address is given as Barangay Hanib on the Basco–Mahatao National Road, and it is also called the Mahatao View Deck or Chanarian View Deck. Mahatao is listed as about
13 km
from Basco, around
30 minutes

by car, and the viewdeck is the first or second stop on most South Batan loop routes. The road winds over a pass and the sea suddenly opens up at the point where the viewdeck stands, so first-time visitors tend to stop in their tracks at the view.

From the viewdeck you take in the western sea (the West Philippine Sea), sea cliffs where waves burst, and rolling green hills that curve into the distance. According to one trip report, there is a shrine in the form of a Virgin Mary grotto and concrete benches, and you can see the rugged western cliff line running south along the road. When waves slam into the rocks the sea glows turquoise, so one guide advises timing your photo to the moment a wave breaks. You may also see grazing cows and goats.

A steep concrete stairway of about 100 steps runs from the viewdeck down to the shore below the cliff. One trip report says people dip their feet, take photos and fish at the bottom of the steps, and that a small pool forms at low tide. But the steps are very slippery when it rains, and a 2017 trip report says the stairs were destroyed by a typhoon and calls the area accident-prone, advising you to bring a guide. Accounts differ on the current state of the stairs, so it is important to check on site.

This guide is for travelers who set out from Basco to tour South Batan in a day. The viewdeck itself takes only about 30 minutes, but linking it with Mahatao Church, Tayid Lighthouse, Diura Fishing Village and Racuh a Payaman (Marlboro Country) makes for a full-day route. Admission fees and opening hours are not given in the sources and it is generally known as an open viewpoint, so check weather and safety conditions locally. One trip report's South Batan day route went like this: in the morning, in Mahatao, the Chawa viewdeck, the church, Tayid Lighthouse, Diura village and Racuh a Payaman; after lunch, through Imnajbu, Alapad, Uyugan and Ivana, ending at the House of Dakay and the Honesty Coffee Shop. The sights are close together along the road, so you can link them easily by car or tricycle. Staying too long at the viewdeck pushes back the rest of the day, so after you have had your fill of the view, set a time and move on.
From the viewdeck the western sea, sea cliffs, breaking waves and rolling hills fit in a single frame. Strong winds blow on many days, so crouch low and take photos from a safe spot.
When waves crash against the rocks the water glows turquoise. One trip report advises waiting for the moment the waves break before pressing the shutter. Burst mode works well.
The viewdeck has a small shrine to the Virgin Mary and concrete benches where you can sit and take in the view. It is a good place to rest for a while and listen to the waves.

About 100 concrete steps lead down below the cliff. You can watch the waves from the shore, but the steps are slippery when it rains and the climb back is breathless. Check the condition locally and go with a guide.

Some sources say there is a "Chawa Cave" near the shore, described as an enchanted cave with a natural salt bed. How to reach it and how safe it is differ by source, so ordinary travelers should not go without a local guide.

The road up to the viewdeck is described as a pass cut into the mountainside (the Alapad section), with the sea and grassland opening on both sides. Pass slowly by tricycle or car and enjoy this scenic stretch.
Cows, goats and carabaos graze on the nearby hills. One trip report saw two mountain goats on a steep slope. Do not approach or feed the animals.
Set out from your Basco lodging by tricycle or van. Going early means softer light and fewer people.
Arrive at Chawa Viewdeck, look out over the cliffs and sea, and take photos near the shrine and benches.
Look at the condition of the stairs and the weather and decide whether to go down. If you do not, enjoy the scenery on foot along the road.
Head toward Mahatao Church and Tayid Lighthouse.
Look around Diura Fishing Village and Racuh a Payaman (Marlboro Country).
Mahatao town is close to Chawa Viewdeck, so you mostly make short hops by tricycle or van. Distances differ by source, so check locally.

items.title: Full-day South Batan route
items.subtitle: Continuing to the Ivatan stone-house villages

children.text: Leave Basco heading south and look around Chawa Viewdeck as the first stop.
Visit Mahatao Church, Tayid Lighthouse, Diura village and Racuh a Payaman in turn.
Have lunch at a restaurant in Mahatao or near Vayang. One trip report lists lunches at about ₱300–375 per person.
In the afternoon head toward Ivana to see the House of Dakay and the Honesty Coffee Shop.
Return to Basco, rest and have dinner.
The afternoon route is long and the day is tight. Delays can happen, so leave some slack.
Take a domestic flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Basco Airport (BSO). Wikipedia says PAL Express operates the Manila route.
Small turboprop aircraft are used and flights are often cancelled in bad weather, so leave extra days in your schedule.
Round-trip fares vary greatly by season, and examples of about ₱10,000–20,000 have been reported.
There are reports that the pre-registration procedure for visiting Batanes has changed, so check provincial government announcements before you leave.
From Basco, travel south along the national road toward Mahatao, about
13 km
and around
30 minutes
by car.
Include it in a tricycle tour or book a van and guide through your lodging. Trip reports from 2018 and 2020 and a recent tour guide put a South Batan tricycle tour at about
per tricycle for two (some operators ask up to about ₱2,000), and one 2018 example of a group tour at about
Some travelers rent a motorbike or bicycle. The winding pass and strong winds can be demanding for beginners.
Public transport is scarce outside Basco, so it is better to arrange your transport in advance.

Wikivoyage describes the best time for Batanes as the dry season of roughly March–June, when winds and waves calm down. In this period there are fewer cancellations and you can enjoy the sound of the waves and the views safely. Basco is known to have its heaviest rain in August–September, and June–July are the hottest months.

Chawa Viewdeck is a cliff facing the western sea, so it tends to be windy, and the steps are very slippery when it rains. In typhoon season, not only visiting the viewdeck but getting around at all may be difficult.

There is almost no lodging around Chawa Viewdeck, and most travelers stay at guesthouses in Basco town and visit on a day tour. There are small lodgings in Mahatao and Ivana as well. Wikivoyage advises that Basco is the only place on Batan with banks, so bring plenty of cash. When booking lodging, it is convenient to be introduced to a South Batan tour driver at the same time. In the low season some restaurants and shops may be closed, so some travelers bring a packed lunch.

Lunch is reported near Mahatao Church or at restaurants near Vayang. One trip report lists lunch at a restaurant within walking distance of Mahatao Church at about ₱300 per person, and one on top of the Vayang hills at about ₱375. Operations change often, so check ahead. Food is expensive because many ingredients are imported.
The wind is strong, so hold your hat and light belongings firmly and do not stand at the cliff edge. Check your footing first even when taking photos.
When waves hit the rocks the water glows turquoise. Use continuous shooting to catch the timing.
The steps are very slippery after rain. Ask a local guide or your lodging about their condition, and do not go down if they are not safe.
Wear shoes with non-slip soles, and bring water, sunscreen and a light waterproof jacket.
Starting the South Batan loop at Chawa Viewdeck gives you more breathing room. Early in the morning there are also fewer people.
Mobile signal is weak in some stretches, so save maps offline in advance.
Show respect in front of the grazing animals and the Virgin Mary shrine. Take your trash with you.

A South Batan loop covers many places in one day, so in seasons when the sun sets early the afternoon is tight. See Chawa Viewdeck in the morning and narrow the afternoon down to two or three places you most want to see.
The cliff edge and the stairs down to the shore are high-risk places for accidents, slippery in rain, and the stairs have been destroyed by a typhoon in the past.
Reaching Chawa Cave and the shore is dangerous depending on waves and rocks. Do not go down without a guide.
The viewdeck faces the western sea and is very windy on many days. Hold children's hands and keep them away from the railing.
In typhoon season roads close and waves become high. Do not visit when weather warnings are issued.
Outside Basco, ATMs and mobile signal are unreliable. Prepare cash and offline maps.
There are reports that Batanes visitor rules, including pre-registration, are changing. Check official announcements before you leave.

An Ivatan-style church whose first stone building dates to about 1789 and whose present structure is said to have been rebuilt in 1873 after a typhoon; the National Museum declared it a National Cultural Treasure in 2001. It is close to Chawa Viewdeck, so link it on the South Batan route.
A hexagonal lighthouse in Mahatao that is fun to compare with Basco Lighthouse. It can also be seen from afar from Racuh a Payaman and Diura village.
The most photographed grassland scenery in Batanes, with blue sky, hills and grazing cows and carabaos. Walk down for even better views.
An overview of all of Batanes, with its rolling grassy hills, stone-house villages and lighthouses. Check it first when planning your itinerary.
Sabtang Island to the south is famous for its Ivatan stone-house villages. You cross by morning boat from Radiwan Port in Ivana.
